project.name: abilities-for-fluent-plugins
project.description: WordPress Abilities API integration for the Fluent plugin ecosystem (FluentCRM, Fluent Forms, FluentBoards, etc.).

nodes.name: Registrar.php
nodes.summary: Core registration helper that eliminates boilerplate from Fluent ability module files by auto-injecting annotations, permission callbacks, and REST visibility from compact per-ability config before calling wp_register_ability().
nodes.languageNotes: PSR-4 class under WickedEvolutions\AbilitiesForFluent\Core; wraps execute_callback closures to cast stdClass input to arrays and emits a typed WP_Error for anonymous CLI denials.

nodes.name: Registrar
nodes.summary: Per-module ability registrar exposing read/write/delete helpers that derive WordPress Abilities API annotations (readonly, destructive, idempotent) and permission callbacks from operation type and compact config.

nodes.name: register
nodes.summary: Internal method that expands compact config into full wp_register_ability() args: builds annotations from operation type, wires capability- or level-based permission callbacks, casts stdClass input to arrays, and conditionally includes output_schema.

nodes.name: denial_for_anonymous_cli
nodes.summary: Builds the denial response for anonymous CLI/stdio invocations, returning a typed WP_Error with migration guidance when no WordPress user is resolved, and plain false otherwise to preserve the bool permission_callback contract.

nodes.name: Phase2RegistrationTest.php
nodes.summary: PHPUnit suite verifying FluentBoards Phase 2 ability registration: confirms research slugs register, read/write/delete annotation semantics, anonymous CLI denial, array property items definitions, and the fluent-boards category binding.

nodes.name: FluentBoardsPhase2RegistrationTest
nodes.summary: Test case asserting that newly added FluentBoards abilities register with correct annotations, categories, schemas, and anonymous CLI denial behavior.

nodes.name: test_anonymous_cli_is_denied_for_every_new_ability
nodes.summary: Verifies that every newly registered FluentBoards ability denies anonymous WP-CLI invocations, asserting the permission callback returns a typed WP_Error rather than true.

nodes.name: CartV2RegistrarSemanticsTest.php
nodes.summary: PHPUnit suite exercising the Registrar against FluentCart v2 abilities: checks read/write/delete annotations, manage_options capability overrides, permission rejection, pagination/list/success schema helpers, and payload shapes.

nodes.name: CartV2RegistrarSemanticsTest
nodes.summary: Test case driving Registrar read/write/delete directly and asserting FluentCart v2 category binding, annotation semantics, capability overrides, and schema helper outputs.

nodes.name: PlayerRegistrationTest.php
nodes.summary: PHPUnit suite validating bulk registration of the 103 Player abilities: asserts all register, no duplicate slugs, per-slug shape and naming conventions, and read/delete annotation correctness via a data provider.

nodes.name: PlayerRegistrationTest
nodes.summary: Test case using setUpBeforeClass to register Player abilities once, then asserting registration count, slug uniqueness, ability shape, naming conventions, and annotation flags across an expected-slug data provider.

nodes.name: expected_slugs
nodes.summary: Returns the canonical list of expected Player ability slugs used by the data provider to assert complete and correct registration.

nodes.name: test_ability_shape
nodes.summary: Asserts that each registered Player ability exposes the expected structure: label, description, callable execute/permission callbacks, category, and meta annotations.

nodes.name: RegistrarTest.php
nodes.summary: PHPUnit suite unit-testing the Registrar in isolation: legacy class alias, read/write/delete annotation injection, show_in_rest, default vs explicit category, input/output schema serialization, and capability overrides.

nodes.name: FluentRegistrarTest
nodes.summary: Focused unit test for the Registrar covering annotation derivation, category defaulting, REST visibility, schema serialization, and capability override behavior.

nodes.name: ci.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions CI workflow that runs PHPUnit unit tests and a deterministic Layer 1 contract gate across a PHP 8.1-8.5 matrix on pushes and PRs, then builds and uploads a release ZIP on tag refs.
nodes.languageNotes: Matrix strategy with fail-fast:false fans out unit tests over five PHP versions; build-release-zip is gated by an if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/') condition and needs both test jobs.

nodes.name: unit-tests
nodes.summary: Runs the PHPUnit Unit testsuite across a PHP 8.1-8.5 matrix after checking out the repo, setting up PHP, and installing Composer dependencies.

nodes.name: contract-gate

nodes.name: build-release-zip
nodes.summary: Tag-gated job that installs production-only Composer dependencies, packages the plugin into a versioned distribution ZIP, and uploads it as a GitHub release asset; depends on unit-tests and contract-gate.

nodes.name: ability-gap.yml

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README — it opens with "Welcome, Wordpressnaut" and lays out the whole mission: exposing the Fluent plugin ecosystem (FluentCRM, Fluent Forms, FluentBoards, Fluent Booking, FluentCart, Fluent Community, Fluent SMTP) through the WordPress Abilities API. It documents the supported products, conditional module loading, MCP client connection paths, installation, and the four-layer permissions/security model. Read this first to build the mental map the rest of the tour fills in.

tour.title: Plugin Bootstrap
tour.description: The main plugin file is the runtime entry point and the top of the dependency graph. It defines constants, registers the PSR-4 autoloader, loads the shared infrastructure (categories, helpers, schemas, security, licensing), and then — on the plugins_loaded hook — conditionally loads ability modules only for the Fluent products that are actually active. Everything else in the tour is something this file pulls in.
tour.languageLesson: WordPress plugins boot from a single header-commented PHP file. Hooking heavy work to 'plugins_loaded' (rather than running at file-load time) lets the plugin detect which sibling plugins are present before deciding what to register — the basis of this project's conditional module loading.

tour.title: The Registrar: Boilerplate-Eliminating Core
tour.description: This is the heart of the architecture and the single most depended-upon component in the codebase. The Fluent_Abilities_Registrar wraps WordPress's wp_register_ability() and exposes compact read/write/delete methods that auto-build the full argument set — annotations, permission callbacks, pro-gating, and input casting — from a tiny per-ability config. Every module from Step 7 onward leans on it, which is why understanding it now makes the rest of the tour read like filling in a template.
tour.languageLesson: This is the Factory pattern in PHP: one class turns terse declarations into the verbose, repetitive structures a lower-level API demands. The PSR-4 version lives under namespace WickedEvolutions\AbilitiesForFluent\Core in src/, the legacy global-named copy under includes/.

tour.title: Shared Helpers and Schemas
tour.description: Two utility libraries every ability module reuses, building on the Registrar from Step 3. helpers.php handles user resolution, error formatting, collection/paginator normalization, and active-module detection; schemas.php provides JSON-schema builders for list, collection, item, and success outputs so every ability speaks a consistent input/output shape. Together they ensure 100+ ability files stay uniform instead of each reinventing pagination and response formatting.

tour.title: Categories and the Security Layer
tour.description: Before any ability can be registered it needs a category to belong to and a permission gate. ability-categories.php registers one Abilities API category per Fluent product via wp_register_ability_category, giving the taxonomy that groups everything. security.php is the core enforcement layer: capability maps, per-module permission checks, module-enabled toggles, and SSRF-safe URL validation. This is the code behind the README's four-layer permissions model.
tour.languageLesson: The Abilities API mirrors WordPress's own taxonomy idea: abilities are grouped under registered categories, and each ability declares a permission_callback. Centralizing those callbacks in one security file keeps capability logic out of the 100+ scattered ability definitions.

tour.title: Licensing and Pro-Tier Gating
tour.description: The suite has a free core and a Pro tier, and three small files coordinate that split. license-manager.php is a singleton that activates/deactivates licenses against a remote vendor endpoint and tracks Pro status with grace-period handling; tier-gate.php's fluent_abilities_pro_gate() wraps a callback so an ability only registers/runs when Pro is active; compat.php is the shim that aliases the namespaced Registrar back to its legacy global name so older module files keep working. These mechanics are invoked throughout the ability modules you meet next.

tour.title: Ability Modules: The Simple Pattern
tour.description: Now the payoff. FluentCRM and Fluent Forms show the canonical module shape in its simplest form: instantiate the Registrar for the module, then declare read abilities (contacts/lists/tags/segments for CRM; forms/entries/submissions for Forms) in a few compact lines each. Compare these to Steps 3-4 and you'll see the boilerplate the Registrar absorbed — these files are almost pure declaration.

tour.title: Ability Modules: Hub-and-Spoke
tour.description: Larger products use a hub-and-spoke layout. boards/abilities.php hooks wp_abilities_api_init, instantiates the Registrar once, defines core board/task/stage/comment CRUD, and exposes a shared $reg scope that its many sub-files (labels, subtasks, time-tracking, webhooks, etc.) extend. cart/abilities.php does the same for FluentCart — products, orders, customers, subscriptions — plus a shared money-formatting helper. This is how the project scales one module to dozens of ability files without duplicating setup.

tour.title: Admin Dashboard
tour.description: The bootstrap also loads a WP-admin surface. dashboard.php renders the Abilities Explorer: it enumerates every registered Fluent ability, offers module/subcategory/type/search filtering, a license-management tab, a pro-feature breakdown, and debug info. It's the human-facing window onto everything the modules from Steps 7-8 registered, and where a site owner manages the Pro license from Step 6.

tour.title: Governing Principles and Security Policy
tour.description: This project is unusually contract-driven, and two documents explain why. PRINCIPLES.md is a binding WordPress-compatibility contract — 11 rules covering registry-first design, native APIs, layered permissions, namespaced metadata, and stable ability contracts — that constrains how every module is allowed to behave. SECURITY.md defines the vulnerability-reporting process and exactly what is in and out of scope. Read these to understand the discipline behind the code you just toured.

tour.title: Vendor Maps and Contract Tests
tour.description: How does the suite prove it stays faithful to the real Fluent plugins? Vendor-map JSON files like fluent-crm.json document each upstream ability's REST endpoint, HTTP method, and canonical controller — a drift detector against the vendor's own surface. RegistrationIntegrityTest.php is the enforcement: a contract test asserting the booted ability set exactly equals a manifest fixture and that every ability has a callable callback. REGISTRAR-DEVELOPMENT.md ties them together as the development playbook for adding modules safely.
tour.languageLesson: Contract tests differ from unit tests: instead of checking one function's logic, they assert the system's externally-visible surface (here, the full set of registered abilities) matches a frozen manifest — catching accidental additions, removals, or renames before they ship.

tour.title: Build and CI Capstone
tour.description: Finally, the automation that holds it all together. composer.json declares the package, the PSR-4 autoload mapping to src/, the PHP requirement, and the dev tooling (PHPUnit, php-parser, opis/json-schema) plus test scripts. The GitHub Actions workflow runs the PHPUnit unit suite and a deterministic Layer 1 contract gate across a PHP 8.1-8.5 matrix on every push and PR, then builds and uploads a release ZIP on tag refs. This is where the principles from Step 10 and the contract tests from Step 11 become enforced gates rather than good intentions.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions matrix builds (here PHP 8.1 through 8.5) run the same job across multiple language versions in parallel, catching version-specific breakage. Tag-triggered jobs ('on push tags') are a common release pattern: routine commits run tests, while version tags additionally build and publish the distributable artifact.
